Definition: Integration of passport issuance and immigration control data into the exchange platform
Comments: Mali has biometric passports issued by IDEMIA through a PPP with MSN subsidiary since 2015 (10-year BOT contract). The passport system is linked to the NINA biometric database - fingerprint matching confirms one person/one passport. In Feb 2025, Mali launched a digital platform for diaspora to access administrative/identity/travel documents online across diplomatic/consular missions. The passport system is the most digitally advanced government ID system but it is managed by a private concession rather than a fully government-integrated data exchange. Score 3: under development toward integration.

Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: Law No. 2013-015 on Personal Data Protection (original) was adopted in 2013, amended in 2019 and replaced/strengthened by Law No. 2024-027 of December 13, 2024. The new law criminalizes data breaches. Constitution of July 23, 2023 recognizes personal data protection. Mali Numerique 2020 included planned e-government laws (cybercrime, cryptography, e-commerce). However, no specific cross-government data sharing law or interoperability law found. Score 2: data exchange mentioned in broader strategy/data protection law but no dedicated enabling legislation for cross-government data sharing.

Definition: Current operational status of the data exchange system
Comments: Mali has no unified national data exchange platform. The country has a NINA (National Identification Number) biometric system, and sectoral platforms including Sigui-Dolo (transport/driver licensing), OpenClinic (health), SIGIP (territorial administration), and TrÃ©sorPay (payments) launched or expanded in Sep 2025. These are isolated sector-specific systems without an operational interoperability hub. USAID's Digital Ecosystem Country Assessment (DECA, 2022) identified 'absence of technical foundational blocks' in digital government. Mali Numerique 2020 strategy (2016) planned 50 public services online but implementation was evaluated as unsuccessful by the government itself. A new strategy for 2023-2027 was under development. Status: planned/early sectoral development, no unified data exchange system.

Definition: Extent to which the data exchange enables services accessible to all population groups including persons with disabilities, elderly, low literacy
Comments: Mali scores 0.3005 on the 2024 UN EGDI, significantly below the African average of 0.4247. Internet penetration is 35.1% (2025). Digital literacy is low nationally. The country faces challenges of territorial vastness, violence in some regions, and limited infrastructure. New platforms launched in Sep 2025 do not include documented accessibility features. Score 1: limited accessibility.

Definition: Provisions ensuring national control over government data and protecting against unauthorized foreign access
Comments: Law No. 2024-027 (December 2024) on personal data protection includes data protection provisions. Constitution of 2023 constitutionally recognizes data protection rights. Mali launched its Feb 2025 diaspora platform described as strengthening 'digital sovereignty'. However, the passport system is managed by a private foreign concession (IDEMIA/MSN). No specific data localization or strong enforced data sovereignty provisions documented. Score 2: limited controls.
